title: The General Arrives
summary: At a temporary Los Lagartos camp in Cinder Basin, an itinerant brotherhood greets Brandon as General Diaz, the absent authority whose return is supposed to settle a bitter succession dispute. Brandon's attempt to pass through only increases their certainty.

panelPlan.text: Wide camp beneath patched shade cloths and the ribs of a half-buried Sunforge. Los Lagartos stop eating, gambling and arguing when Brandon, Eva and Jessie enter.
An older member stands and addresses Brandon as General Diaz. Several others rise with relief; a rival cluster rises with anger.
Brandon keeps walking toward the water table. Jessie quietly changes direction toward the exit. Eva slows, openly interested in the recognition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Could somebody point me toward water before I become a third person?

title: A Vote Nobody Wants
summary: Los Lagartos insist that 'Diaz' settle whether the group follows an older blood claim or a younger elected leader. Brandon refuses to choose, but every refusal is interpreted as the general testing them.

panelPlan.text: Two sides of the camp face each other across a long communal table. Brandon has been placed at the head despite repeatedly moving his chair sideways.
Speakers from both sides make concise cases. Eva watches the group more than Brandon, noticing how everyone edits themselves in his presence.
Brandon finally stands, moves the head chair out of the way and sits on a water crate at the side, physically refusing the role.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I was afraid you'd say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Los Lagartos
dialogueInline.text: Blood claim or the vote. Say which stands.

dialogueInline.speaker: Los Lagartos
dialogueInline.text: Because you left us with the choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Los Lagartos
dialogueInline.text: Diaz would know what he meant.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm sure he would. I don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They think you're making them prove something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm trying to get out of the chair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That's why they think you're making them prove something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm more worried about the gun.

title: The Woman Behind Them
summary: Eva notices Raina questioning camp members about Brandon. Raina reveals that she already has more identities attached to Brandon's face than Eva and Jessie have encountered, making clear that her investigation predates their awareness of it.

panelPlan.text: At the edge of camp, Raina steps into the dispute. Eva watches from behind a shade post; Jessie catches Eva watching.
Raina turns and catches Eva's stare. She approaches rather than pretending she was not observing them.
Jessie steps between them only enough to make the boundary clear. Raina looks past her toward Brandon at the communal table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: The gun is the easy part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Raina James. How long has he been Brandon?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Long enough to answer the question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: No. Long enough to repeat his answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I have four names and the same face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: If you think he's lying, ask him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Sounds like you want that to be enough.

title: What Diaz Would Do
summary: A confrontation inside Los Lagartos turns violent when one claimant tries to force the decision. Brandon intervenes to prevent a killing, and the group immediately treats his action as Diaz's judgment.

panelPlan.text: A younger Lagarto draws on an older rival across the campfire. Conversation dies; nearby people freeze and look between the gun, the two rivals and Brandon.
Brandon knocks the muzzle aside with a tin cup before the shot clears leather. Sand Rider, a real local scout, pins the shooter's wrist without ceremony.

The crowd's insistence that Brandon's intervention 'isn't enough' carries Raina's challenge forward and turns stopping the gun into a supposed judgment. Brandon looks at Sand Rider, then at the two claimants, irritated that stopping a murder has become constitutional law.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: He was about to shoot a man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then Diaz and I agree on one thing. Don't shoot people across dinner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: They can call it supper if they put the gun away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: You are going to have a long day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I was beginning to suspect that.

title: No General
summary: Brandon turns the group's need for Diaz back on them: if they cannot choose without a dead man's authority, then Diaz's return would only postpone the fight. The community makes its own decision while Brandon prepares to leave.

panelPlan.text: Brandon, already resigned to a long day, stands outside the head position at the table and returns the old general's signet or token that someone pressed into his hand.
The two claimant groups face each other without Brandon between them. Jessie has the rig ready; Eva lingers close enough to hear.
One Lagarto moves the head chair away entirely. Others follow, reshaping the circle rather than crowning a winner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then help me shorten it. Where is Diaz?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then you have a problem he can't answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Leave before somebody else draws a gun.

title: A Name in the Dust
summary: As the trio leaves Cinder Basin, Eva learns that Los Lagartos were told to expect General Diaz by a traveling preacher several days earlier. Raina watches the departure from behind them, making the pattern feel less accidental without yet proving coordination.

panelPlan.text: The rig pulls away from camp as Eva says she did take something useful from the encounter: the preacher arrived first. Eva runs alongside for two steps after asking one last question, then catches the rear rail.
She tells Brandon and Jessie that a preacher described Diaz before their arrival. Jessie looks back through the dust.
Far behind, Raina stands where the camp road narrows, not following yet. Near her, a black Sunforge rib catches the light. Brandon never looks back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I did. I got something better than an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The preacher got here three days before us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He told them Diaz would have black hair, a dark coat, and deny being Diaz.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The last part is less nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You are working very hard to make this boring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm working very hard to keep bad guesses from becoming facts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Good news. I can hear you.
